Am I Using AI to Extend My Thinking, or Avoid It?

Every powerful tool changes what we practise. The real question is what happens when convenience begins to replace the struggle that develops judgement.

SAGE for AIJuly 1, 20262 min read
#AI#Judgement#Learning

My mom used to say: “Anything in excess is poison.” I didn’t think much of it when I was younger. But over time, I started noticing something. I used to remember phone numbers. I used to do quick mental math. I used to sit with problems longer before reaching for help. Then smartphones arrived. They didn’t make me less intelligent. They simply removed the need to practice those small habits. Now I see a similar shift happening again. At a workshop recently, a speaker said something that stayed with me: “Generative AI optimizes for the statistical average.” Whether taken literally or not, the idea made me pause. Because LLMs are incredibly powerful. They can retrieve, summarize, connect, and generate at a speed no human can match. But every powerful tool changes what we practice. Calculators changed arithmetic. GPS changed navigation. Search engines changed memorization.

So the question becomes: What will LLMs change in us? The more I use them, the more I notice a subtle shift. I reach for answers faster than I sit with questions. I sometimes generate before I think through the problem. And it makes me ask myself: Am I using AI to extend my thinking… or to avoid it? Because the value was never just the answer. It was the struggle required to reach it. I don’t worry about AI becoming smarter than me. I worry about becoming too dependent on something that isn’t thinking at all.
